FX-GTINT-001.says: Tint One Colour, orange, radius 12, everything else at Soft Physical Glow's defaults: the yellow, brown and purple patches all glow orange.

FX-GTINT-002.says: Tint Core to Edge at its defaults, white core and blue edge, radius 12: white close to each patch, turning blue as the glow spreads.

FX-GTINT-003.says: Core to Edge, radius 100: seven levels, so the change from white to blue runs over more steps.

FX-GTINT-004.says: Core to Edge, Tint Amount 50: halfway between the glow's own colours and the tint.

FX-GTINT-005.says: Core to Edge, Tint Amount 0: the glow's own colours, the same as Soft Physical Glow with no tint (FX-SGLOW-001).

FX-GTINT-006.says: Tint Off written in the file, with colours set: Soft Physical Glow as before (FX-SGLOW-001).

FX-GTINT-007.says: One Colour, orange, on the drawing with a grey patch: the grey glows orange too, as brightly as a colour of its brightness would.

FX-GTINT-008.says: Core to Edge, orange core and purple edge, Threshold 30 in Luminance: only the yellow glows, orange near it and purple further out.

FX-GTINT-009.says: Core to Edge, radius 0: nothing spreads; the light laid on itself takes the core colour, white, so each patch brightens towards grey-white.

FX-GTINT-010.says: Core to Edge, radius 2.25: the one level, half in, is the widest, so it is blue, and the half laid on itself is white.

FX-GTINT-011.says: Tint Amount keyed from 0 at frame 0 to 100 at frame 4, linear: frame 0 is FX-GTINT-005, frame 2 is FX-GTINT-004, frame 4 is FX-GTINT-002.

FX-GTINT-012.says: Core to Edge, Blend Mode Add, exposure 3: the tinted light adds up past white.

FX-GTINT-013.says: Core to Edge, Unmult off, Source Opacity 0: the tinted glow alone, on black.

FX-GTINT-014.says: Core to Edge, Aspect Ratio 1.5 at Angle 30, moved three pixels right: the leaning glow tinted, and the layer grown to hold it.

FX-GTINT-015.says: Core to Edge, the patches half covering: the light counts at half, so the tint is half as bright.

FX-GTINT-016.says: Core to Edge, radius 2,000: on a drawing this small the wide blue levels spread their light far past the frame, so what stays is mostly the small, near-white levels: a faint wash, white touched with blue.

FX-GTINT-017.says: Tint "duocolor", which is not off, one_color or core_to_edge. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-GTINT-018.says: Inner Colour "#12345", not six hexadecimal digits. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-GTINT-019.says: Outer Colour "blue", not a colour word the file takes. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-GTINT-020.says: Tint Amount 101, above 100. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-GTINT-021.says: Tint Amount -1, below 0. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.

FX-GTINT-022.says: Tint Amount keyed to 150 at frame 4. The file is read, the effect is kept as written and left out of every frame, with a warning.
